## About

I am a fifth-year PhD student in Economics at the University of Mannheim and a
researcher in the Department of Corporate Taxation and Public Finance at the
[ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research](https://www.zew.de/en) in
Mannheim.

My research is in **public economics**, with a focus on **public finance** and
**political economy**. On the revenue side of public budgets, I analyze understudied
tax instruments, such as second-home and tourism taxes, and how they affect tax
avoidance, public finances and housing markets. I also study public debt and how
it interacts with monetary policy in the euro area. Beyond tax design, I work on
tax administration and the role of digitalization in revenue collection. On the
expenditure side, I look at how political incentives shape public investment
decisions.

Beyond my topical focus, I work on empirical methods: I use large language models
and web-scraped data to measure economic variables, and I develop research
software and inference methods for machine learning techniques.
